<div align="center">
    <h1>
        Zabbix ClamAV Template
    </h1>
    <h4>
        Monitoring ClamAV daemons, signature database and scan results via Zabbix Agent
    </h4>
    <br>
</div>
<br>
<br>

<!-- *********************************************************************************************************************************** -->
<!-- *** BODY ************************************************************************************************************************** -->
<!-- *********************************************************************************************************************************** -->
## Description
This template monitors ClamAV on Linux hosts via Zabbix Agent: the `clamd` and `freshclam`
daemons, the freshness and integrity of the signature database, and the results of the scheduled
scan read from its log.

- **Signature database** - the agent returns the plain-text output of `sigtool --info` through a
  UserParameter; the template converts it to JSON and exposes its fields through dependent items.
  The build time detects a stale database, the signature verification result raises a
  high-severity alert when it is not `OK.`.
- **Daemons** - `proc.num` counts the running `clamd` and `freshclam` processes.
- **Scan log** - active log items read the file your scheduled scan appends to: one `FOUND` line
  per infected file, and the `SCAN SUMMARY` block of every finished scan.

## What is monitored
- **clamd and freshclam** - number of running processes, alert when a daemon is not running
  (hosts without the daemon set the minimum to 0).
- **Database freshness** - build time of the installed ClamAV signature database, with warning and
  high-severity thresholds.
- **Signature database** - signature count and ClamAV database version.
- **Database verification** - digital signature verification result (`OK` or `FAIL`).
- **Infected files** - counter of `FOUND` lines in the scan log, the lines themselves (file and
  signature), alert when a file was found in the last `{$CLAMAV.INFECTED.PERIOD}`.
- **Scan results** - infected files, scanned files and duration of the last finished scan, alert
  when no scan finished for `{$CLAMAV.SCAN.NODATA}`.
- **Collectors** - no-data alerts for the database info and for the scan log.

## Requirements
- **Zabbix 7.0 or higher**
- Linux host with **Zabbix Agent** or **Agent 2**, reachable on its agent interface (the database and process items are passive checks) **and** active checks configured (`ServerActive` and `Hostname`; the scan log items are active checks)
- ClamAV with `sigtool` and a signature database kept up to date by `freshclam` (`/var/lib/clamav/daily.cld` or `daily.cvd`)
- A scheduled scan (`clamscan` or `clamdscan` with `--log`) appending to `/var/log/clamav/scan.log`, or any other file you put into `{$CLAMAV.SCAN.LOG}`
- The `zabbix` user must be able to read the signature database and the scan log

## Setup
### 1. Check that sigtool and the database are there
ClamAV keeps the daily signature database as `daily.cvd`, and as `daily.cld` once `freshclam` has
applied the first incremental update. The command uses whichever of the two the host has, and runs
`sigtool` as the `zabbix` user - exactly what the agent will do later:
```bash
f=/var/lib/clamav/daily.cld; [ -f "$f" ] || f=/var/lib/clamav/daily.cvd; sudo -u zabbix /usr/bin/sigtool --info "$f"
```
The output starts with `File: /var/lib/clamav/daily...` and has to end with `Verification OK.`. If `sigtool` is missing, install ClamAV first
(`sudo dnf install clamav clamav-update` or `sudo apt install clamav clamav-freshclam`) and run
`sudo freshclam` once.

If the command fails with *Permission denied*, let the agent account read the database:
```bash
sudo usermod -aG clamav zabbix
```

### 2. Prepare the scan log
`clamscan` and `clamdscan` create their log with mode `0640`, owner `root`, which the agent cannot
read. Give the file the `zabbix` group once - the scan keeps appending to it, and an existing log
keeps its content:
```bash
sudo mkdir -p /var/log/clamav
sudo touch /var/log/clamav/scan.log
sudo chown root:zabbix /var/log/clamav/scan.log
sudo chmod 0640 /var/log/clamav/scan.log
sudo -u zabbix test -r /var/log/clamav/scan.log && echo readable
```
The answer has to be `readable`.

If the host has no scheduled scan yet, add one - this example scans `/home` every night at 02:30
and appends the result to the log:
```bash
echo '30 2 * * * root /usr/bin/clamscan --recursive --infected --log=/var/log/clamav/scan.log /home >/dev/null 2>&1' | sudo tee /etc/cron.d/clamav-scan
```
A scan you already have only needs `--log=/var/log/clamav/scan.log` added to its command, or the
macro `{$CLAMAV.SCAN.LOG}` on the host pointed at the file it writes - readable by `zabbix` the same
way.

### 3. Download agent config (pick Agent or Agent 2)
Download **only one** file (`clamav.conf`). It defines the `clamav.status` UserParameter and picks
`daily.cld` or `daily.cvd` by itself, whichever the host has.

Zabbix Agent
```bash
sudo wget https://git.initmax.cz/initMAX-Public/zabbix-templates/-/raw/production/free/ClamAV_by_Zabbix_agent/7.0/clamav.conf -O /etc/zabbix/zabbix_agentd.d/clamav.conf
sudo chown zabbix:zabbix /etc/zabbix/zabbix_agentd.d/clamav.conf
```

Zabbix Agent 2
```bash
sudo wget https://git.initmax.cz/initMAX-Public/zabbix-templates/-/raw/production/free/ClamAV_by_Zabbix_agent/7.0/clamav.conf -O /etc/zabbix/zabbix_agent2.d/clamav.conf
sudo chown zabbix:zabbix /etc/zabbix/zabbix_agent2.d/clamav.conf
```

The file holds a single line:
```text
UserParameter=clamav.status,f=/var/lib/clamav/daily.cld; [ -f "$f" ] || f=/var/lib/clamav/daily.cvd; /usr/bin/sigtool --info "$f"
```

### 4. Check that active checks are configured
The scan log items are active checks: the agent reads the file itself and sends the result to the
server named in `ServerActive`, under the name in `Hostname`. Print both lines:

Zabbix Agent
```bash
grep -E '^(ServerActive|Hostname)=' /etc/zabbix/zabbix_agentd.conf
```
Zabbix Agent 2
```bash
grep -E '^(ServerActive|Hostname)=' /etc/zabbix/zabbix_agent2.conf
```
`ServerActive` has to name your Zabbix server or proxy, and `Hostname` has to be exactly the host
name the host has in Zabbix. An empty answer means the two lines are missing - add them to that file.

### 5. Restart agent
Zabbix Agent
```bash
sudo systemctl restart zabbix-agent
```
Zabbix Agent 2
```bash
sudo systemctl restart zabbix-agent2
```

### 6. Test items
Zabbix Agent
```bash
sudo -u zabbix zabbix_agentd -t clamav.status
sudo -u zabbix zabbix_agentd -t 'proc.num[clamd]'
sudo -u zabbix zabbix_agentd -t 'proc.num[freshclam]'
```
Zabbix Agent 2
```bash
sudo -u zabbix zabbix_agent2 -t clamav.status
sudo -u zabbix zabbix_agent2 -t 'proc.num[clamd]'
sudo -u zabbix zabbix_agent2 -t 'proc.num[freshclam]'
```
The first answer has to contain the `Build time`, `Version`, `Signatures` and `Verification OK.`
lines. The two counters answer `[s|1]` when the daemon runs. `[s|0]` for `clamd` means the host
scans with `clamscan` only - set `{$CLAMAV.CLAMD.PROC.MIN}` to `0` on the host after the import;
`[s|0]` for `freshclam` means the updater runs from cron - set `{$CLAMAV.FRESHCLAM.PROC.MIN}` to `0`.

### 7. Import template
Import [`template_clamav_by_zabbix_agent_7.0.yaml`](./7.0/template_clamav_by_zabbix_agent_7.0.yaml)
(**Data collection -> Templates -> Import**) and link it to the host. The host needs a Zabbix agent
interface.

### 8. Check the result
After the first polling interval (`{$CLAMAV.INTERVAL}`, one hour by default - use **Execute now** on
the `ClamAV: Database info RAW` item to skip the wait) the database and process values show up in
**Monitoring -> Latest data**, filter by tag `component: clamav`, `clamd` or `freshclam`.

The scan items (tag `component: scan`) only see lines appended after the agent picked them up, so
they fill in when the next scheduled scan finishes. To see them now, run one small scan:
```bash
sudo /usr/bin/clamscan --infected --log=/var/log/clamav/scan.log /etc/hostname
```
Within a minute `ClamAV: Last scan: Infected files` shows `0`, `Scanned files` shows `1` and
`Duration` shows how long the scan took. `ClamAV: Infected files detected` reports `0` every
minute as long as the log gets no `FOUND` line.

### Macros used
| Macro | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `{$CLAMAV.CLAMD.PROC.MIN}` | Minimum number of running `clamd` processes; `0` on a host that scans with `clamscan` only | `1` |
| `{$CLAMAV.FRESHCLAM.PROC.MIN}` | Minimum number of running `freshclam` processes; `0` on a host that updates from cron | `1` |
| `{$CLAMAV.INFECTED.PERIOD}` | How long the "Infected files detected" problem stays open after the last `FOUND` line | `1d` |
| `{$CLAMAV.INTERVAL}` | Interval for reading the ClamAV database information | `1h` |
| `{$CLAMAV.NODATA}` | Time without data before the no-data warnings (database info, scan log) are raised | `3h` |
| `{$CLAMAV.SCAN.LOG}` | The log file the scheduled scan appends to, read by the active log items | `/var/log/clamav/scan.log` |
| `{$CLAMAV.SCAN.NODATA}` | Time without a finished scan before the no-scan warning is raised; keep it above the scan interval | `2d` |
| `{$CLAMAV.UPDATE.HIGH}` | Database age at which the high-severity alert is raised | `7d` |
| `{$CLAMAV.UPDATE.WARN}` | Database age at which the warning is raised | `3d` |
